item.title: Nigeria: At least 24 dead after boat capsizes
item.description: The boat carrying mourners for a funeral overturned in southern Nigeria. It was the latest in a series of deadly boat accidents in the country.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Getting rid of antibiotic resistance: Challenges and possible solutions
item.description: If antibiotics stop working, even the smallest infection can be fatal. The WHO expects millions of deaths over the next 25 years. Can the "One Health" approach help combat antibiotic resistance?
item.dc:subject: NRS-Import

item.title: Mexican special forces arrest drug kingpin 'Chapo Isidro'
item.description: The alleged leader of the Beltran Leyva gang and one of the FBI's most wanted fugitives, known as 'Chapo Isidro,' was captured by the Mexican military following a raid and a shootout in the coastal Sinaloa state.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Russian helicopter suspected of violating Finnish airspace
item.description: Finland's Defense Ministry thinks the incursion is linked to a drone strike earlier Saturday on a Russian cargo ship, which is on a US sanctions list.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: EU and Indonesia sign trade deal
item.description: A deal covering 730 million people promises lower tariffs and new investment opportunities as the European Union seeks to diversify trade ties amid growing global economic tensions.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: New EU budget proposal aims at tax gobal tech giants
item.description: European Council President Antonio Costa has proposed a smaller EU budget for 2028-2034, including a 3% tax on major digital firms to ease member states' contributions. France has already rejected the plan as inadequate.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Russia strikes Zelenskyy's hometown, killing 2
item.description: The attacks follow Russian President Vladimir Putin's vow of a "painful" response to Ukraine's attacks this week on the Kerch Bridge, linking Russian-occupied Crimea.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Germany's religious freedom report: Authoritarian regimes, holy wars, and spies abroad
item.description: Harassment, persecution, surveillance: Across much of the world, people of faith are facing growing pressure. A new German government report is unusually direct in criticizing China in particular.
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: COP31: UN Climate summit runs into overtime as deal remains elusive
item.description: After nearly two weeks of negotiations, countries remain divided on how to fight global warming. Nations are now eyeing a third and final draft text. DW has more.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Anthropic researcher uses AI to solve math's greatest riddle
item.description: The proposed breakthrough could reshape mathematical research, but still needs independent verification. It's the latest in a string of cases where AI has outpaced humans in solving famous maths problems.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Germany news: Support for Ukraine military aid waning, survey shows
item.description: Nearly half of Germany's population wants to reduce military aid to Ukraine, a survey has found. Meanwhile, German consumers are set to pay more in energy bills next year due in part to the Iran war. DW has more.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: 'Killer robots' talks at UN end with no legally binding ban
item.description: Countries have agreed to extend discussions over controls on lethal autonomous weapons systems for two years.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: US judge jails Indian national in foiled Sikh separatist murder plot
item.description: New Delhi has denied any role in the plot to kill Sikh separatist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun in New York. Meanwhile, over 200 people have been hospitalized after consuming spurious liquor in Manipur state. DW has more.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Man convicted of arson over deadly 2025 Palisades fire in Los Angeles
item.description: A 30-year-old man has been convicted of causing one of the most destructive wildfires in the history of Los Angeles. The verdict came after the case was retried.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Three El Salvador soldiers die in explosives accident in Haiti
item.description: The soldiers were part of a Salvadoran military contingent deployed to the violence-ridden Caribbean nation last month to rescue four missing airmen. The deployment has widened into an operation against Haiti's gangs.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Brazil ex-President Jair Bolsonaro taken to hospital over abdominal pain
item.description: Jair Bolsonaro has been hospitalized in Brasilia with intestinal obstruction. The former far-right Brazilian leader is receiving pain medications, his son Carlos said.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: UK anti-migrant activist jailed for slashing Channel dinghy
item.description: Daniel Thomas, known as "Danny Tommo," slashed a dinghy with a knife while a French rescue worker was on board. The incident was livestreamed to a large social media audience amid growing tensions over migrant crossings.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: US judge approves Bayer's $7.25 billion cancer settlement
item.description: Bayer could end years of costly lawsuits in the US over claims that its Roundup weedkiller causes cancer. Tens of thousands of people could now receive compensation, although some lawyers say the payments are too low.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Russian ornithologist jailed over small donations to Navalny's foundation
item.description: Sofia Rosenfeld has devoted her life to studying Arctic birds. A Russian court sentenced her to 3.5 years in a penal colony over donations to Navalny's foundation. Friends and family are fighting for her release.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Repression against Iranian lawyers increases
item.description: At least 135 lawyers in Iran have been subjected to repressive measures over the past year. UN experts warn that this seriously jeopardizes the right of those accused to trial in a constitutional court.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: COP31: No agreement on climate science, disinformation spreading
item.description: Attacks on climate science and disinformation risk delaying key measures at COP31 in Antalya. As the UN climate talks draw to a close, how will that affect efforts to come to an agreement?
item.dc:subject: Environment

item.title: Has the 'Parthenon puzzle' been solved? The long quest to reassemble lost eastern pediment
item.description: The depiction of the birth of the goddess Athena above the Parthenon's entrance is considered a masterpiece of ancient art. Now, a German research team has pieced together all the surviving fragments.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: Better educated than ever — yet Germany's Gen Z is being shut out of its own future
item.description: Never before have young people around the world been so well-educated while facing so many economic challenges. Young Germans are asking: Will I be better off than my parents?
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: Can German auto manufacturing recover after Mercedes and VW cuts?
item.description: German automakers are pulling back on investments at home, sparking fresh anxiety about the auto sector's future. Some industry watchers think there is still a narrow window to stem the decline. But how?
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Measles in America: Here's a constructive approach to beating the disease, based on Brazil's experience
item.description: The US is now officially a measles contagion zone. By mid-2026, there were more infections than in all of the previous year. But the country could beat measles again, just like Brazil did two years ago.
item.dc:subject: Science

item.title: Germany face Belgium in Nations League quarterfinals — Klopp plays down favorites tag
item.description: Germany coach Jürgen Klopp is looking to "carry positive momentum forward" as his team draw neighboring Belgium in the quarterfinals of the UEFA Nations League.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: EU and UK strike 'landmark deal' to strengthen ties after Brexit
item.description: The European Union and the United Kingdom have agreed on "landmark" deals on youth mobility and trade. Leaders on both sides praised the agreement as they seek to rebuild ties.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Turkey takes control of opposition broadcaster Sozcu TV
item.description: In the latest in a series of raids and arrests, another major pro-opposition Turkish broadcaster has been brought under state control. This is the third in a year.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: FIFA presidential election 2027: Infantino facing Diallo and Tashima — could an alliance change everything?
item.description: Two challengers to Gianni Infantino have registered for next year's FIFA presidential election. What do Philippe Diallo and Kozo Tashima stand for – and do they stand a chance against the incumbent?
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Lufthansa to cut 1,000 jobs, citing ongoing losses — reports
item.description: According to a letter obtained by the media, Lufthansa's executive board said the German company is losing €20 million every month. In addition to job cuts, operational cuts are also planned.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Have we missed our chance to stop climate change?
item.description: From record-breaking heat to devastating floods and wildfires, the warning signs are everywhere. Can rising temperatures still be brought under control?
item.dc:subject: Climate

item.title: Putin proposes second humanitarian ceasefire — is it a trap?
item.description: Russian President Putin has suggested evacuating civilians from the embattled Ukrainian city of Kostiantynivka. But experts warn this could serve military, not humanitarian, aims. What should Kyiv do?
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Uganda minister at COP31: 'We need a just transition'
item.description: Funding from wealthy countries to help deal with the impacts of climate change hasn't materialized, says Uganda's environment minister. The East African country is hoping oil and carbon credits will help boost finances.
item.dc:subject: Climate

item.title: No mention of fossil fuels in latest COP31 draft deal
item.description: One of the most fraught debates at the UN climate talks in Turkey has revolved around the future of coal, oil and gas. Now, all mention of fossil fuels has been removed from the summit's new draft agreement.
item.dc:subject: Environment

item.title: Anthropic trading tests investors' appetite for AI
item.description: Anthropic was valued at $2 trillion after shares started trading on the Nasdaq following a record $81 billion IPO. Its performance will put investor confidence in AI to the test.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Alexander Zverev faces fresh lawsuit from ex-girlfriend
item.description: World No. 1 tennis player Alexander Zverev is facing a new lawsuit related to a domestic abuse trial. The lawyer for his ex-girlfriend, Brenda Patea, told DW what the allegations are against the German player.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: EU Commission confirms it was targeted in cyberattack using AI tools
item.description: The European Commission was targeted by an "AI-generated cybercampaign," a spokesperson has said. This is the first time the bloc has publicly reported an AI-based cyberattack.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Wadephul: 'Coalition of the Willing' talks in Berlin send strong signal to Moscow
item.description: German Foreign Minister Wadephul has said the Coalition of the Willing meeting in Berlin sends a clear message to Moscow to take peace talks seriously. He also warned Ukraine should be prepared for peace talks to fail.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Iran balances ties with China and Russia as Trump ramps up pressure
item.description: As Donald Trump seeks to tighten economic pressure on Iran, China remains its biggest oil customer and Russia a key partner. But both powers are balancing support for Tehran against broader interests with Washington.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Is the AI bubble bursting just as Anthropic goes public?
item.description: The sharp sell-off in tech stocks after the US midterms and the Nvidia scandal has cast doubt on Anthropic's IPO. Yet with hundreds of billions still being invested, some think the AI party is still in full swing.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Borussia Dortmund bows to fan pressure and end Rheinmetall deal
item.description: Borussia Dortmund has reluctantly ended its association with a major sponsor after long-term fan protests. They are not the first Bundesliga club to u-turn, as commercial interests clash with politics and fan culture.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: 'Coalition of the Willing' meets in Berlin: Europe remains committed to Ukraine
item.description: The "Coalition of the Willing" supporting Ukraine is gathering in Berlin. One of the key issues under discussion is whether Europe will be able to play a role in future negotiations over the country's future.
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: How a green economy could help reverse climate change
item.description: Green growth promises a future in which economies thrive without destroying the environment. But is this vision realistic?
item.dc:subject: Environment

item.title: Hashim Thaci's second conviction in The Hague reignites debate in Kosovo about justice and the Kosovo Specialist Chambers
item.description: Former President Hashim Thaci has been convicted of trying to influence witnesses in his war crimes trial. The conviction has reignited debate in Kosovo about the Kosovo Specialist Chambers, the court that convicted him.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Back to 1997: Russia wants NATO to roll back its eastern expansion
item.description: The Kremlin is reportedly calling on NATO to withdraw from large parts of Eastern Europe. What this would mean for the security of millions of Europeans — and what lies behind Russia's plan.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Rights court rules Turkey must release jailed lawmaker Atalay
item.description: The European Court of Human Rights has called for the release of imprisoned elected lawmaker Can Atalay. Atalay has been in prison for almost five years despite rulings from the Turkish Constitutional Court.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Nvidia forms national security committee after Huang affair
item.description: Nvidia has created a board-level committee for national security and export control. This follows the resignation of CEO Jensen Huang over extramarital affairs, allegedly including one with a Chinese intelligence asset.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Students' List candidates take seats as Serbian parliament opens
item.description: Serbia's Student List's candidates have taken their oaths in the inaugural parliament session. As the new majority, they have 90 days to form a government.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Klopp and Wirtz offer glimpse of bright German future
item.description: Germany's fall from grace in recent years has seen the team drift away from the fans. But Monday's drubbing of the Netherlands and the impact of Jürgen Klopp, Florian Wirtz and emerging youngsters offers hope.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Could the Airbus €3 billion loan row reignite a US-EU trade dispute?
item.description: The US says a record €3 billion financing package for Airbus may conflict with a transatlantic aircraft-subsidy truce. EU officials insist the funding complies with market-based rules.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Germany news: Plans for Rwanda migrant hub come under fire
item.description: Human rights groups have slammed plans by Germany and four other EU states to send rejected asylum seekers to Rwanda. In other news, business start-ups in Germany are on track to reach the highest level since 2015.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: France's Philippe Diallo to challenge Infantino for FIFA presidency
item.description: Philippe Diallo is the second candidate to stand against incumbent Gianni Infantino. He is backed by European football's governing body UEFA, known to be critical of Infantino.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: NASA's Voyager 1 reaches a light-day away from Earth
item.description: When just saying 'hello' takes a two-day round trip, you're a light-day, or 26 billion kilometers, from Earth. Only one human-made object has ever traveled that far — and its journey into interstellar space continues.
item.dc:subject: Science

item.title: What has changed in James Bond films over the decades
item.description: In 1962, a martini-drinking womanizer saved the world for the first time in "Dr. No." As Robert Pattinson takes on the role of 007, here's how the films evolved.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: The AfD and neo-Nazi networks: How close are the connections?
item.description: The Alternative for Germany party (AfD) has become a focal point for the far right. Many of its members and staff have ties to ethnonationalist or neo-Nazi organizations.
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: COP31 draft deal calls for 'immediate' shift away from fossil fuels
item.description: The preliminary agreement at UN climate talks in Turkey calls for a rapid reduction of planet-warming emissions and at least $120 billion to help countries adapt to climate change.

item.title: Klopp wants Infantino out as FIFA candidate deadline looms
item.description: Germany coach Jürgen Klopp has joined the chorus of football figures critical of FIFA President Gianni Infantino. But with time running out, there are few who seem willing to run against him.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Germany news: Merz, Söder aim to revisit electricity tax cut
item.description: The Christian Democrats are in Munich, pushing to revive some tax relief that didn't make it into the budget after talks last week. And Manuela Schwesig faces a vote on a new term as regional leader. Follow DW.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Can a 'coalition of the willing' create momentum for a fossil fuel phaseout?
item.description: In April, about 60 countries held an unprecedented meeting in Colombia to work out a plan to slowly quit oil, coal and gas. How influential is this coalition at the COP31 climate summit?
item.dc:subject: Environment

item.title: AI in classrooms: Fighting the great 'dumbing down'
item.description: Research suggests that students who aren't careful about how they use ChatGPT and other AI tools risk poorer academic outcomes. It's a huge challenge for teachers.
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: German economy returns to growth, so why is the country still worried?
item.description: The German economy is growing again, albeit slightly. However, economists warn that without reforms, higher productivity and solid public finances, a loss of prosperity and growing debt threaten future generations.

item.title: Despite restrictive abortion laws, Poland's 'Abortomat' — a locker that dispenses abortion pills — helps women who want to end a pregnancy
item.description: Abortion laws in Poland are very restrictive. Activists there have found a new way to help women wanting to terminate a pregnancy: the "Abortomat," a locker that dispenses abortion pills. But they face fierce opposition.

item.title: Germany news: Germany holds national day of remembrance
item.description: Events were held for "Volkstrauertag," a day commemorating victims of war and oppression. Meanwhile, experts said the country is headed for a budget crisis.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: How AI is likely to change Germany's job market
item.description: The scale of the economic disruption caused by AI has led even conservative politicians to talk about universal basic income. But economists aren't convinced, and campaigners think we need to ask deeper questions.
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: Germany's 2027 budget: A record €561 billion and a mountain of debt
item.description: The 2027 federal budget proposal has finally been hammered out and is set for a vote in parliament. What are the government's policy priorities in defense, infrastructure, the economy and social spending?
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: Werner Holzer Prize awarded to Katja Gloger and DW's Jaafar Abdul Karim
item.description: DW journalist Jaafar Abdul Karim and Russia correspondent Katja Gloger have been awarded the prestigious Werner Holzer Prize for international journalism.

item.title: Ukraine: Zelenskyy says security deal could go to referendum
item.description: The US has broached the idea of Kyiv giving up the Donbas region in exchange for NATO membership, the Ukrainian president said.

item.title: Wolf Biermann at 90: The singer who defied East Germany
item.description: His life is a reflection of contemporary German history, addressed via his songs and sharp wit. At 90, he's as feisty as ever.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: Turkey uses espionage accusations to pressure government critics
item.description: The arrest of a German foundation's employee in Istanbul this week has put the focus back on pressure tactics used by the Erdogan administration. The arrest is far from the first of its kind.

item.title: Gen Z protests: Do Baby Boomers really have it better than young people?
item.description: Should young people in Germany be more worried about their future than Baby Boomers were in the 1980s and 1990s? Or should both generations take to the streets and protest together? DW checked the data.

item.description: Experts warn against revising Europe's security framework because they say it would mean granting Moscow its longstanding wish of renegotiating postwar security on the continent.

item.title: What's going on with the polar vortex?
item.description: Observations show the ring of fierce winds that rotate at the Earth's North Pole has changed direction. Scientists say it's a historic disruption and the earliest reversal on record. What could it mean for the weather?
item.dc:subject: Environment

item.title: Ice hockey impasse as Russia threatens sanctions on Canada, Germany
item.description: Two weeks after the CAS ordered ice hockey's governing body to reintegrate Russia into international play, a solution remains elusive. Now Russia has threatened to take legal action against two tournament hosts.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Germany gives sweeping powers to police, intelligence services
item.description: Drone sightings and cyberattacks have heightened security concerns. How are the police preparing to meet these challenges? And how do intelligence services plan to counter threats from both domestic and foreign sources?
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: Germany's Nmecha won't repeat controversial goal celebration
item.description: Germany head coach Jürgen Klopp has said midfielder Felix Nmecha will not repeat a goal celebration that sparked controversy over the past week. Germany are set to face Serbia and the Netherlands in the Nations League.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Germany news: Parliament agrees on debt-laden 2027 budget
item.description: The budget committee in the Bundestag worked into the night to sign off on next year's spending plans. These include levels of new debt only eclipsed once, at the height of the COVID pandemic. DW has more.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Czechia braces for massive protest against public media reform plans
item.description: A fast-tracked bill to cut public media funding has sparked strikes, rallies and fears for the independence of public broadcasting in Czechia. A massive protest is planned for Prague on Sunday.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Could lack of money sink TFFF rainforest fund before it even launches?
item.description: The TFFF rainforest fund aims to make forest conservation more profitable than deforestation. But a lack of money may prevent it from getting off the ground.
item.dc:subject: Environment

item.title: Iranian activist and Nobel Peace Prize winner Narges Mohammadi shares her story in memoir
item.description: Written and smuggled out of prison, the 2023 Nobel Prize laureate's memoir reveals the cost of defying Iran's regime and fighting for freedom.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: EU leaders tussle over whom to send to Ukraine, Russia peace talks
item.description: A seat at the table for Europe now appears likely following comments by a US envoy who just held talks with Putin. But who will take that seat remains unclear.

item.title: Can the EU make it harder to trick consumers online?
item.description: The EU wants to curb subscription traps, misleading sales tactics and features that keep people scrolling. What would the proposed Digital Fairness Act change, and does it go far enough?
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: What have the talks with Russia and the US in Abu Dhabi achieved for Ukraine?
item.description: The first trilateral talks between Ukraine, the US and Russia in nine months have ended with an agreement on exchanging prisoners. Does this mark a genuine breakthrough and a step toward peace?
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Hungary eases abortion restrictions in women's rights overhaul
item.description: The reforms mark a break the the conservative policies of former PM Viktor Orban. The controversial "heartbeat regulation" is to be scrapped and women are to be better protected against violence.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: UK court convicts 2 Iranian men of spying on journalists
item.description: A London court has found two Iranian citizens guilty of surveilling reporters for a Persian-language television station critical of Iran's government. One was also convicted of planning a violent attack against them.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Jensen Huang: Spy row, affairs leave Nvidia without its rockstar CEO
item.description: Jensen Huang, who built Nvidia into the world’s dominant AI chipmaker, is stepping down as CEO over extramarital affairs. DW examines how losing its figurehead will affect the firm and the US-China AI race.

item.title: What are fossil fuels?

item.title: Germany news: Police raid chapters of Gremium MC biker gang
item.description: Police in southwestern Germany launched major early-morning operations against a biker gang. The state of Baden-Württemberg is outlawing three of its chapters. Meanwhile, unions are planning more strikes.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Bundeswehr study exposes widespread sexual harassment in German military
item.description: Sexual misconduct in the Bundeswehr is far more widespread than previously known, with younger women disproportionately affected. Defense Minister Boris Pistorius has called for a policy of "zero tolerance."
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: Intelligent women get less help at work, study finds
item.description: Women who scored high on intelligence tests were seen as more hostile by their teammates and got less help, a new study finds. High-scoring men faced no such penalty. Research explains why.

item.title: Fears of rising antisemitism in Europe
item.description: Holocaust survivor Regina Sluszny commemorates the victims of Auschwitz as Jewish communities across Europe face growing hostility. What does the promise of "Never Again" mean for Jewish life in Europe today?
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: Why the integration of immigrants in Germany remains a challenge
item.description: The Federal Office for Migration and Refugees has released a new Integration Report. It found that while the integration of people with a migrant background is improving, violent youth remain a problem.
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: Is AIIB's complaint mechanism failing affected communities?
item.description: The Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank has a grievance redress mechanism for people affected by projects it finances. But those seeking to file a complaint face significant hurdles. Critics say reforms are needed.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Wael Mohya could make German football history at 17
item.description: At just 17, Gladbach forward Wael Mohya has earned his first Germany call-up. The dual-national talent has chosen the DFB path for now — and could soon make modern national-team history.

item.title: Can global leaders put their money where their mouth is on climate?
item.description: World leaders warn that geopolitical divisions are distracting from the climate crisis as negotiations focus on clean energy and financing, while Iran calls for compensation for war-related environmental damage.

item.title: DW Science explainer on the default mode network: what your brain does when you aren't focusing on anything, and why it's important.
item.description: Doing nothing might be the ultimate brain hack. When you're bored, the brain goes into default mode network. It's not only healthy for you, but it may also shape the very essence of your identity.

item.title: Germany slips in climate protection rankings as other countries make gains
item.description: Record renewable energy growth is driving climate progress in some countries, but Germany and many major emitters are falling behind.

item.title: Controversial kinship: From colonial rule to the Holocaust?
item.description: Hitler once called Eastern Europe "Germany's India." A new exhibition examines the links between colonialism and Nazism, and the bitter debate over where comparisons illuminate history and where they fall short.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: Neuer injury gives Urbig chance to shape Bayern and Germany future
item.description: Manuel Neuer's latest injury gives Jonas Urbig a run of games in Bayern's goal. Marc-André ter Stegen remains Germany’s No. 1, but Urbig now has a chance to strengthen his case for the future.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Megaspeed and the battle to go high-end Nvidia chips into China
item.description: Jensen Huang's affair with a suspected Chinese spy has shone a light on Megaspeed, the company she worked for. It is under investigation in the US for smuggling Nvidia chips into China, which it denies.

item.title: Borussia Dortmund's Felix Nmecha and the question of religion
item.description: Felix Nmecha's "Crowns down" celebration has drawn criticism from a Borussia Dortmund fan club, reopening debate over faith, inclusion and religious messaging in football.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Why electrification is the climate game changer we need
item.description: From EVs and electric buses on the road, heat pumps warming homes and solar panels powering appliances, the shift to electrifying tech is already in full swing. But what exactly does "electrification" mean?

item.title: Will Australia push for fossil fuel exit at UN talks?
item.description: The heat is on Australia as chief negotiator at the COP31 UN climate conference to forge a path away from coal and gas, and to protect Pacific neighbors facing rising sea levels.

item.title: Why malnutrition can go unnoticed, and what that means for our health
item.description: More than 2 billion people worldwide suffer from nutrient deficiencies, most of them in the Global South. The health consequences can be devastating.

item.title: Iran war oil shock drives dip in global emissions, study shows
item.description: Global carbon emissions are expected to fall slightly in 2026, but not because of major progress on climate action. Instead, it's high energy prices following the US attack on Iran that's driving the trend.

item.title: Norway's ice hockey team says Russia replacing it at World Juniors
item.description: The wrangling over Russia's return to international ice hockey continues, with Norway saying it has been kicked out of the next major tournament to accommodate Russia. Switzerland has joined a "boycott."

item.title: 37 years after fall of Berlin Wall: How divided are Germans?
item.description: Three artists share their thoughts on the reunification of East and West Germany. How do they perceive a shared "we" and what gives them cause for optimism?
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: Why Nvidia CEO's affair with alleged Chinese spy matters for AI race
item.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has apologized for an affair with a woman the US believes was spying for China. The story could have profound implications for the world's most valuable company and the global AI race.

item.title: 'Never Again!': Holocaust remembrance under pressure

item.title: As COP31 Antalya kicks off, can world move beyond big promises?
item.description: Droughts, floods and extreme heat are upping the pressure on delegates at the UN climate talks in Antalya, Turkey. Can countries move beyond pledges to concrete action?

item.title: Germany hopes to host world ice hockey championship — without Russia
item.description: International protests continue after a court ruled that Russia must be allowed to return to international ice hockey. Germany is seeking a solution that will allow the country to host next year's world championship.

item.title: Amid protests, France's rising debt costs threaten stability
item.description: France plans to spend an extra €4 billion on education amid nationwide protests. But with public debt mounting and interest costs climbing, how much fiscal room does the government have?

item.title: Tesla to 'wind down' production of flop Cybertruck
item.description: Elon Musk's electric pickup for the future will start to be consigned to the past next year. The Cybertruck's bulk and crude shape meant it could only pass regulatory standards in more permissive markets.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Preparing for 45C: How Germany tests its crisis response
item.description: A record heat wave. Five years of drought. A nation under pressure. Germany is running its biggest joint crisis exercise to date to test how authorities would cope with an escalating climate emergency.
item.dc:subject: Environment

item.title: What to know about the IIHF Women's Ice Hockey World Championship
item.description: As ice hockey's governing body continues to wrangle over how to respond to a CAS order to reinstate Russia to international play, the top women's tournament gets underway in Denmark without Russia.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Exercise coaching boosts colon cancer survival
item.description: Evidence suggests exercise can keep more cancer patients alive. But what does "living longer" actually mean, and who does it apply to?
item.dc:subject: Science

item.title: European shares join a global sell-off as AI spending fears rattle Wall Street and Asian markets
item.description: European shares have fallen after sharp losses in Asia and on Wall Street. Doubts over huge AI investments and fears of curbs following the Democrats' US midterm victory have rattled global markets.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Russia is back in world sport, but who is drug testing its athletes?
item.description: DW has found that three-quarters of Russia's weightlifting team had no independent out-of-competition testing before this year's world championships, despite the country's doping history.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Cristiano Ronaldo announces retirement from international football
item.description: The announcement by the footballing legend comes just weeks after a public spat with Portugal coach Jorge Jesus over playing time.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: What the Democrats' midterms win means for the US economy and Trump
item.description: From high oil prices and data centers to tariffs and mounting debt, economic concerns played a key role in the crushing defeat of President Donald Trump's Republicans. So can the Democrats now make a difference?
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Gold for the West Bank: Meet Palestinian karate champ Mariam Bsharat
item.description: The occupied West Bank is not an obvious breeding ground for sporting success. But Mariam Bsharat, 17, has beaten the odds to become a karate world champion and is making a new life in Germany.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Harry Potter films turns 25 ahead of new TV series' release
item.description: In 2001, "Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone" hit cinemas and took the world by storm. Today, anticipation for the new series is high, but its creator, J.K. Rowling, remains a controversial figure.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: Leading ice hockey nations, sponsors oppose Russia's return
item.description: Ice hockey's governing body says the impact of a court decision forcing it to reinstate Russia presents "significant practical and sporting challenges." Several leading nations say they won't play against Russian teams.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: BMW reports lower Q3 earnings as China woes mount
item.description: BMW reports a drop in profits in the July to September quarter amid fierce competition from China.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Germany's celebrated children's author Janosch has died
item.description: Bear, Tiger and Tiger-Duck: The author and illustrator Janosch achieved world fame with his heartwarming children's figures. He died at the age of 95.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: Could AI give NFTs a second chance?
item.description: NFTs have plunged in value since their pandemic height in 2021. In some cases, they are worth 99% less than they were paid for. Yet tokenization of real-world assets and AI means the curios may yet have a future.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: From rotten food to political opponents: Researchers explore how disgust relates to our beliefs, and why the connection is complicated
item.description: Some studies have linked disgust sensitivity to socially conservative attitudes. But does disgust shape our politics, or do our beliefs shape what we find disgusting?
item.dc:subject: Science

item.title: How Berlin's Arab queers are building their community
item.description: As the co-founder of the ADIRA Drag Festival, Lebanese performance artist, drag performer, DJ and cultural organizer Hassandra has become an essential part of Berlin's queer artistic landscape.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: Football: Spanish player dies on after cardiac arrest on the pitch
item.description: Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel has died following a collision with the opposing goalkeeper. The Spanish second-division club has said it is "heartbroken" by the loss.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Asian Cup postponed due to Middle East conflict
item.description: The Asian Cup has become the latest sporting event to be affected by the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. Organizers cite "exceptional circumstances" in Saudi Arabia, which has seen several Houthi attacks of late.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Could the AI boom make borrowing more expensive in Europe?
item.description: France, Germany and Italy face a volatile bond market as war inflation bites. With US tech giants now issuing billions in AI bonds, they are competing with cash-strapped European governments.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Ice hockey officials considering options after CAS order to reinstate Russia
item.description: Ice hockey's ruling body is deciding how to respond to a decision by the Court of Arbitration for Sport that allows Russia back into international competition. Germany hasn't ruled out pulling out as a tournament host.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: LA communities kick out Big Oil
item.description: After years of advocacy from residents and legal battles with Big Oil, Los Angeles voted to ban drilling and phase out oil extraction in the city. It's the first city in the United States to kick the oil industry out.
item.dc:subject: Environment

item.title: Embarrassing name? How we live with names we don't like
item.description: What happens when your name evokes laughter or ridicule? Research points to negative life outcomes, but some people learn to embrace unfortunate names.
item.dc:subject: Science

item.title: Germany news: Merz hopes for Korean reunification at DMZ
item.description: Chancellor Friedrich Merz has expressed hope for Korean reunification during a visit to the heavily fortified border. Meanwhile, President Steinmeier has held talks with China's Xi Jinping in Beijing.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: The dachshund, a humorous icon with political symbolism
item.description: From Picasso to Andy Warhol, a surprising number of artists have portrayed the German breed. But the dachshund has also at times been co-opted as a political symbol.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: 'Star Trek' star Patrick Stewart dies age 86
item.description: The Shakespearean actor landed the role of a lifetime as "Star Trek" Captain Picard. He passed away at age 86.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: India increases growth forecast for fiscal year
item.description: India's Ministry of Finance has increased its growth forecasts for the current fiscal year. But it also warned about inflation, particularly for fuel and energy, amid continued instability in the Middle East.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Volkswagen logs Q3 operating loss of €5.86 billion on Porsche writedown
item.description: The Volkswagen Group has filed its worst quarterly performance since the height of the "Dieselgate" scandal in 2015. Share prices climbed in response, however, perhaps because the bad news was so well signposted.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Can we regrow damaged seagrass meadows?
item.description: Seagrass protects coasts, shelters thousands of species and stores CO2. But some 30% of this valuable ecosystem has disappeared since the late 19th century. Can we bring it back?
item.dc:subject: Environment

item.title: EU moves to loosen rules on pesticide use as experts sound the alarm
item.description: The European Union wants to relax rules for pesticides, saying it will be easier for farmers to adopt more environmentally friendly options. But health and environmental experts say the risks are far too great.
item.dc:subject: Environment
